answer: No single shop can bless a forgery: the proof must survive three keepers who never meet. Curing a proof takes 9 days, and a farm holding 763 proofs cannot cure them side by side. A timber bought at noon, a hollow borrowed by dusk, a velvet that takes a season: the farm owns the first two and will never hold the third. This epoch the gate asks one thing only: Flour merchant millet meal milled at the millrace, and the receipt must read each millet is a season of logged millings plus a signed millhouse record. The farm sells volume, the epoch buys proof, and the two never meet.
